subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK (streaming, function calling, embeddings)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK (streaming, function calling, embeddings)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the same priorities captured:

Key pain points you shared:
- Search result reranking is slow and inconsistent with increasing query volume (current pipeline spikes latency up to ~800ms).
- Need streaming responses for the in-product chat UX to reduce perceived latency and show partial answers.
- Desire structured outputs + function calling for extracting actions from chat (e.g., create-ticket, route-to-team).
- Want embeddings + reranking for semantic search across product docs and support tickets; must be compatible with your existing vector store.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Reduce 95th percentile latency for reranking to <= 300ms for typical queries.
2) Ship a streaming chat PoC in your web UI within 4 weeks.
3) Validate embeddings-based reranking quality on your benchmark set (sample set we discussed).

Integration / product fit notes:
- SDK: our JS/TS SDK already supports streaming and function-calling primitives. For your client-side chat, we recommend Server Sent Events (SSE) or WebSocket forwarding via server proxy; the SDK has an example for both.
- Function calling: Redwood supports structured outputs with typed schemas; the SDK can return a parsed JSON payload and optional token-level metadata for provenance.
- Streaming: continuous token streaming is supported; we also have prefix-KV caching to reduce cost for repeated context.
- Embeddings/Reranking: we produce 768- and 1536-dim embeddings (model choices). We can provide a side-by-side comparison export to your vector store. Reranking can be implemented as a two-stage pipeline (dense retrieval -> model-based rerank).
- Auth / networking: Hosted API works for initial PoC. If you need private networking/VPC, Redwood Private can be scoped later; we discussed bringing in security after we validate quality.

Attachments provided:
- mutual-action-plan.xlsx (proposed milestones, owners, dates)
- redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf (sample code & streaming/function-calling examples)
- acme-requirements.docx (internal requirements)

Next steps / owners:
- Marissa: schedule integration workshop (I can run a 60-min SDK + streaming workshop) — action: schedule by EOD Thursday (Jul 16).
- Alex: share the sample query set and target latency SLOs (by Fri Jul 17).
- Rachel: follow up on security questionnaire and any AD/SSO requirements.

Would you confirm these and add/update any owners? Happy to jump on another quick call to walk through the SDK examples.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 21:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK (streaming, function calling, embeddings)

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and captures our priorities. A few clarifying points before we commit to the workshop:

- Latency SLO: our current internal target is 95p <= 300ms end-to-end for the reranking step alone (post-retrieval). Is that achievable with the Redwood hosted reranker or would we need Dedicated capacity for predictable tails?
- Embeddings: we use a custom reranking pipeline built on top of Milvus. Can you confirm the exact dimensions and floating-point format (fp16/int8) you export? We'll need to validate compatibility and storage sizing.
- Streaming: for our front-end, SSE is preferable, but we also have a proxy that can open a WS tunnel from our servers. Any performance tradeoffs between SSE vs WS vs your streaming REST endpoint we should consider?

I've attached our internal requirements doc (acme-requirements.docx) and a short architecture note we discussed. If you can answer the three bullets above, we can lock the workshop time.

Best,
Alex
Director, AI Platform — Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com | (212) 555-0166

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK (streaming, function calling, embeddings)

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and for sending the requirements. Short answers inline below, and I've included a link to a short code sample in the shared Drive.

- Latency SLO: Hosted reranking can meet 95p <= 300ms for your expected qps at PoC scale in most regions; for strict enterprise tails and guaranteed throughput we'd recommend Redwood Dedicated. I can run a quick perf simulation against a sample of your queries (we do this in ~48 hours) and share tail percentiles.

- Embeddings export: we provide embeddings in float32 by default; optional fp16 and quantized int8 exports are available depending on model. We can export 768-d or 1536-d vectors. We'll coordinate with your Milvus team to confirm encoding and compression settings.

- Streaming: SSE is simple and works well for browser clients (lower connection overhead). WebSockets can reduce latency on high-concurrency UIs and allow bi-directional signaling if you need it. Our SDK has both examples — link below. For the PoC, SSE + server-side proxy is a safe default.

Code samples and quick perf-run checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AExampleSharedDrive (see redwood-streaming-example.js)

Proposed timing:
- Integration workshop: Fri Jul 17 at 11:00am PT — 60 minutes (I will demo SDK streaming + function-calling + embedding export). Please confirm or suggest an alternative.
- I will start the perf simulation as soon as you share the sample query set (Alex).
